#2079. “Welcome Back” Paco On The Market Following Dismissal | West Ham News

Former West Ham assistant coach Paco Jémez is once again searching for a new club after being relieved of his duties by Moroccan giants Raja Casablanca following a disappointing start to the season.

Jémez earned admirers for the attacking brand of football he implemented in Spain, and many supporters pointed to the turnaround in performances at West Ham as being credited to him.

However, his latest managerial venture has come to an abrupt end after Raja Casablanca opted to make a change just over two months after appointing him.

The club confirmed that Sunday’s 2-0 defeat to RS Berkane would be Jémez’s final match in charge, with officials deciding a fresh approach was needed after reviewing the team’s performances and results.

An official club statement explained that the sporting management felt a change in technical leadership was necessary to provide a new dynamic and improve the club’s chances of meeting its objectives this season.

Despite arriving in Casablanca with an impressive CV that included spells at Rayo Vallecano, Granada, Las Palmas and Mexican side Cruz Azul, the Spaniard struggled to generate momentum. Raja collected just six points from their opening five league fixtures, winning once, drawing three times and losing once.

Those results left his new club down in 13th place and under growing pressure, a situation made worse by a run of performances that failed to convince supporters.

Reports in Morocco had suggested Jémez’s future was already under scrutiny before the defeat against Berkane, with the coach reportedly asking club officials for more time to improve results. However, the latest setback proved decisive.

Following the defeat, Jémez accepted responsibility and apologised to supporters, acknowledging that the team had not produced the level of performance expected from one of Morocco’s biggest clubs. He also stated that he would accept whatever decision the board deemed appropriate.

West Ham ultimately went in a different direction by appointing Rui Pedro Silva as assistant head coach in the summer, despite Jémez publicly stating he wanted to stay on. Yet as of this morning, things have moved on!

Jémez’s latest dismissal serves as a reminder of the ruthless nature of football management.

A coach once regarded as one of Spain’s most innovative tacticians now finds himself looking for a fresh opportunity after another short-lived spell in the dugout.

For me, he’d always be welcome back at West Ham in a coaching capacity as part of Scott Parkers new regime.

#2078. Rangers learn match officials for Saturday night Premiership clash vs St Mirren

The match officials have been confirmed for Rangers’ Scottish Premiership trip to St Mirren.

Rangers travel to The Marbill Coaches Stadium on Saturday, November 7, with the league clash scheduled for an 8pm kick-off.

Nick Walsh has been appointed as the man in the middle, with Frank Connor and Daniel McFarlane running the lines. Gary Hanvidge will be the fourth official, while Greg Aitken is on VAR duty with Peter Stuart assisting.

This won't be Walsh’s first involvement with Rangers this season. He took charge of the Premier Sports Cup clash between Rangers and Celtic at Ibrox in September, which Rangers won 3-0.

The experienced whistler had several Rangers assignments last season too. Those included a 1-1 draw away to St Mirren in August 2025, Rangers’ 2-0 League Cup victory over Hibernian, and the 3-1 League Cup defeat to Celtic at Hampden in November.

He was also in charge as Rangers lost 2-1 at Hearts in December, before overseeing their 2-0 home victory against Aberdeen in January.

#2077. Why this season feels so uncertain as a Newcastle United fan

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Hope you are all doing well, I am in my 40s and a long time Newcastle United fan living in Australia.

I eventually got the chance in September to come and see my first game at St James’ Park against Hull – it was brilliant.

I watch all the matches, read, listen to pods etc and have played all my life (I’m 42).

I’m also into the tactical side of things and have undertaken some of my coaching badges here in Australia.

I’m sharing my first submission to The Mag about why I think this season feels so uncertain as a Newcastle United fan.

Newcastle United are a club of ups and downs – we all know that. The club’s current reality feels like we’re on the way down, though in reality it is more like a straight line from last season than any sort of significant change :

2026/27 13th place in the Premier League after 9 games. 11 points in those 9 games at an average of 1.22 points per game. 2025/26 12th place in the Premier League after 38 games. 49 points in those 38 games at an average of 1.28 points per game.

There are lots of reasons that this season feels more ominous than last season, though primarily it’s because we have no clear idea what to expect from this manager and from this group and players. We don’t know what to expect.

For Newcastle United fans, this season is full of unknowns.

Was Eddie Howe keeping our heads above water?

Who on earth are half of these new players?

Could we… go down, or could we actually end up being alright with a few tweaks?

Never in recent years have Newcastle United fans had so much to be uncertain about.

Under the management of Eddie Howe, there was certainty. We knew him and he knew us. There was no chance we were getting relegated under Howe, even through last season’s struggles.

We knew he knew the league. We knew he knew how to win games in this league. We knew he knew the histories, we knew he knew just what a cold, wet night in Stoke meant. We knew he could (mostly) improve players on an individual basis and get the best out of them. We knew the players respected him, liked him and trusted him. We knew his tactics and his style, and we knew they worked (mostly).

We knew Howe’s team. We knew that when the chips were down, Bruno would take the lead. We knew he’d demand the ball, that he’d try with every last ounce of determination and skill to create something, to inspire his teammates and to inspire the fans. We knew big Joe had his back and would kick someone if he had to, or even if he didn’t. We knew we had a threat up front or out wide to hurt opponents. We knew we had guys who could score goals in the Premier League. We knew Tripps wouldn’t stand for a team that didn’t give their all. We knew we had high standards, kept by high quality players who had done it all and seen it all.

Now, all that safety and certainty is gone and you know what – it’s freaking us out. Without the guard-rails that the certainty of Howe provided for us, we’re contemplating the worst. We’re scared of free fall. We’re not cautiously optimistic – we’re venturing towards riotously pessimistic.

So, now, after a similar start to last season in terms of points, we’re worried. Not worried like we were last year – this time it’s different. We’re worried because we’ve got no idea what comes next. We’ve got no idea how Matthias Jaissle responds or what he might do to get a tune out of this team. We’ve got no real indication yet that this group of players can actually deliver at this level, under any manager.

We don’t know how PIF, David Hopkinson and Ross Wilson will respond to this, because they haven’t had to before. We don’t fully know whether they even know what they’re doing to be honest. They seem to for the most part, but here we are nine league games in, with fingernails dwindling, a hard run of games ahead and a bunch of youngsters or also rans to take us through to the derby and Christmas and the crazy winter schedule..,so maybe they don’t know what they’re doing?

So, while we gaze into the unknown, let’s also think about the knowns. We know we’ve got a great set of fans. We know that when St James’ Park is rocking we can get the team over the line against almost anyone. We know this year they might well need that and they’ll need us behind them to succeed in this league.

We know we’re in transition. We know we care. We know we want the team to succeed whoever the manager is, wherever he’s from and whoever is on the pitch. We know it’s going to be turbulent because when has it ever not been? And we also know, we don’t want to support anyone else.

#2076. Erik ten Hag launches latest attack on Cristiano Ronaldo: Former Man United boss claims Portugal star's career was OVER by time he joined Juventus

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 12:32 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 14:19 EDT, 1 November 2026

Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has taken another swipe at Cristiano Ronaldo, claiming the Portugal icon's career was already over by the time he joined Juventus and eventually returned to Old Trafford.

The legendary forward's second spell at United ended acrimoniously after he launched a public attack on the club and Ten Hag, accusing the manager of 'betraying' him in a bombshell interview.

Ronaldo, whose United contract was terminated following his explosive criticism of the club, joined Al-Nassr in January 2023, while Ten Hag was eventually sacked in October 2024 after a disappointing run of results.

Last month, Ten Hag gave a wide-ranging interview to The Athletic in which he criticised Ronaldo for 'letting the team down' and accused the club's hierarchy of contributing to a 'toxic culture'.

The Dutchman has now doubled down on his criticism of the 41-year-old veteran once again, claiming Ronaldo could not 'make way' for the team.

'Every top team must embrace the top player, but the top player must also make way for the team. That was simply the problem with Ronaldo,' Ten Hag said in an interview on ESPN.

Erik ten Hag has claimed Cristiano Ronaldo's career was over by the time he returned to United

Ten Hag conducted a wide-ranging interview with The Athletic last week in which he hit out at the club's hierarchy for contributing to a 'toxic culture' - and lashed out at Ronaldo

'Let there be no misunderstanding on my part, he is of course a great player. He belongs among the greats of the world.

'But the reality is also that he hasn't been able to deliver for the last seven or eight years. From Juventus onwards, it was simply over.'

Ten Hag also praised Real Madrid, where Ronaldo statistically enjoyed the most prolific years of his career, for selling the superstar at what he believed was the perfect time.

'That is also Real Madrid's great gift,' he added. 'They see when a player is declining in level. Then they part ways at a moment when, to the outside world, they are still at their peak, but actually can no longer deliver.'

In Ten Hag's tell-all interview last month, he accused Manchester United's owners of 'breaking promises' over recruitment and blasted them for showing a lack of ambition in the transfer market.

His criticism of Manchester United came amid a turbulent spell for the club, with Lisandro Martinez and Bruno Fernandes both publicly criticising the board and manager Michael Carrick respectively in recent weeks.

Carrick was given a chance to put things right after United's chiefs met for crunch talks earlier this week in the wake of his side losing 4-1 to Como in the Champions League and 3-0 to Bournemouth in the Premier League.

According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo was not prepared to stand aside for the good of the team

Ronaldo, who now plays for Al-Nassr, is within touching distance of scoring 1,000 career goals

On Saturday, United met a similar fate as they were thumped 3-0 by Chelsea at Stamford Bridge, piling even more pressure on Carrick.

Red Devils legend Peter Schmeichel expressed his anger at Ten Hag speaking out against the club during this difficult period last week.

Speaking on The Overlap Daily, former United goalkeeper Schmeichel said: 'What really annoys me in everything that has happened in the past two weeks is Ten Hag coming out and saying that he wanted Declan Rice and Harry Kane, like he was a god.

'It's so ridiculous. He brought (Lisandro) Martinez in, (Matthijs) de Ligt. I mean he brought players in that are still there, how dare he go out and say that.

'Everybody knew we should sign Harry Kane. Everyone knows we should have signed Declan Rice, that's no secret. I don't know why we didn't do that.

'But you have now people stirring the pot where they should just keep calm and not talk and maybe talk about what they did for this football club themselves, or what they didn't do.

'He wasn't a success at Manchester United. Why does he feel the need to come out and say that?

'What he's saying is "I was let down by the club" and there might be an element of truth in that but he wasn't good enough. And then he went to Bayer Leverkusen, a team who had just won the Bundesliga, and then he got sacked within, what, three games?

Ten Hag also hit out at Manchester United's hierarchy amid a turbulent time for the club

Michael Carrick has been given a chance to turn things around after chiefs held crunch talks

'Maybe just take a step back and don't put yourself in that because then you will end up with someone like me criticising him, and there's no need for that. We don't need it in the narrative.'

Ten Hag was sacked by United in October 2024 after a string of poor results left the team 14th in the Premier League.

His future had been in doubt after he led United to a disappointing eighth-placed finish in the top flight a couple of months earlier, but victory in the FA Cup final over rivals Manchester City contributed to the club's decision to give him a contract extension in the summer after crunch talks in Ibiza.

He went on to replace Xabi Alonso at Bundesliga side Bayer Leverkusen the following season, but was sacked after just three games in charge, and he criticised the club's board for this 'unprecedented' decision.

#2075. West Ham Exclusive: Parker’s Promotion Clause And Nuno’s £3m Payoff Revealed

Scott Parker is expected to sign a two-and-a-half-year contract with West Ham United this afternoon, with Claret & Hugh receiving fresh information about the proposed deal and the compensation package for departing manager Nuno Espírito Santo.

A club insider briefed C&H within the last few moments, revealing that Parker’s agreement includes break clauses linked directly to whether West Ham secure promotion back to the Premier League at the first attempt. We have also been informed that Nuno is set to receive just under £3million in compensation following his dismissal this morning.

The details represent a significant development following our earlier exclusive identifying Parker as the leading candidate to replace the Portuguese coach. The former Hammers midfielder now appears close to completing his return to the London Stadium, although the appointment has yet to be officially announced.

It will coast West Ham just under £3m to sack Rui Pedro Silva & Nuno Espirito Santo

According to our source, Parker has been more than happy to accept the proposed terms, with a genuine desire within the club to see him succeed.

Speaking to Claret & Hugh within the last few moments, the insider explained:

“Parker will need to get West Ham up this season. If he doesn’t, he’ll be released without compensation. If he gets promoted to the Premier League, it will activate a two-year deal.”

In effect, Parker’s longer-term future at West Ham will depend upon achieving promotion this season.

Failure to return to the Premier League would allow the club to part company with the manager without paying compensation, according to the information we have received.

Promotion, however, would activate the remaining two years of his contract.

Claret & Hugh have also been informed that Parker will be given the opportunity to manage West Ham in the Premier League should he secure promotion.

That assurance is particularly interesting given his dismissal by Burnley last season, despite having previously guided the Clarets into the top flight.

Parker’s experience of winning promotion with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley appears to have been a significant factor in West Ham’s interest.

The Hammers hierarchy are evidently prioritising a manager with a proven Championship promotion record, while protecting the club financially should their objectives not be achieved.

Meanwhile, Nuno’s departure, confirmed earlier this morning, is expected to cost West Ham just short of £3million in compensation.

The proposed agreement with Parker would therefore represent a very different financial arrangement, with the club’s promotion ambitions written directly into the terms of his employment.

An official announcement confirming Parker’s appointment is still awaited.

#2074. Total Premier League minutes played by the 8 Newcastle United signings tells a story

The independent voice of Newcastle United since 1988

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

Get your daily update and weekly newsletter by signing up today!

A lot of focus on the eight Newcastle United signings that were brought in across summer 2026.

There were actually nine in total but teenager Ousmane Diabate was instantly loaned back to the selling club in Turkey in order to get regular first team football.

So what about these eight Newcastle United signings that have gone straight into the first team squad?

I have had a look at the minutes played so far this 2026-27 season by the new players.

Specifically, the minutes that each of the eight have played in the Premier League.

I think it tells a very clear story now we are nine Premier League matches (810 minutes) into this 2026-27 season.

Total Premier League minutes (out of a possible total of 810) played by the eight Newcastle United signings with breakdown match by match (Ev Everton, CP Crystal Palace, AV Aston Villa, Cov Coventry, H Hull, Le Leeds, B Bournemouth, T Tottenham, Li Liverpool):

0 Ewen Jaouen (Zero minutes in any of the nine Premier League matches)

115 Bazoumana Toure (3Ev, 34AV, 30Cov, 16H, 33Le)

256 Sean Steur (26Ev, 5CP, 66H, 71 Le, 13B, 19T, 56Li)

304 Matias Fernandez-Pardo (56AV, 90Cov, 74H, 57Le, 27B)

501 Nico Gonzalez (64Ev, 90CP, 90AV, 90Cov, 19Le, 77B, 71T)

536 Amar Dedic (87Ev, 90CP, 31Cov, 58Le, 90B, 90T, 90Li)

810 Lukas Hornicek (90Ev, 90CP, 90AV, 90Cov, 90H, 90Le, 90B, 90T, 90Li)

What stands out for me, is that Matthias Jaissle has given far more Premier League minutes to the (relatively) older and more experienced Newcastle United signings.

Three of the eight Newcastle United signings were aged 24 when they arrived, the other five were 21 or under.

Lukas Hornicek has played every Premier League minute this season.

Nico Gonzalez has started all seven EPL matches he has been available for.

Amar Dedic has started all of the EPL matches he was in a position to start, as well as off the bench against Coventry.

The other five Newcastle United signings who were aged 21 and under when they arrived at St James’ Park, have played 702 minutes between them. That is less than Lukas Hornicek alone has played and would also be less than the Dedic and Gonzalez individual totals if they had been available all of the time.

On the other hand, Matias Fernandez-Pardo has played far more minutes than I think he would have otherwise done so far, simply because of so many injured players in the early part of the season.

I am sure that Matthias Jaissle sees the exciting potential of Sean Steur just as much as we do, probably even more so considering he watches him every day in training. However, my belief is that the Head coach is simply trying to protect the 18-year-old from too much expectancy and pressure too soon. The same with the other younger players.

I don’t think he is holding the likes of Toure and Bamba back from playing more minutes so far because of any negative irrational reason, more a case of giving these younger inexperienced players from weaker leagues a chance to integrate and build up their confidence rather than throwing them in at the deep end and a case of sink or swim?

The booing from many Newcastle United fans at the Everton match for example, it isn’t exactly something that will help younger players to build confidence if they are subjected to that.

#2073. Mason Mount offering Michael Carrick a midfield solution which could have legs

It is not uncommon to hear football club executives talking about the importance of the “money being on the pitch”.

In other words, managers having their best players fit and available most if not all of the time. Quality at the top level is essential but so is robustness. They go hand in hand.

Unfortunately for Manchester United, the money has not been on the pitch down the years nearly as much as the club would want or expect.

Bruno Fernandes stands out for what he does with the ball primarily, but also because he plays almost every minute of every game and, while his sheer indefatigability is extreme, United know they need more of his ilk.

This is why the forthcoming season is such a big one for Mason Mount. His quality has seldom been in doubt. The problem is he has rarely been on the pitch long or consistently enough to show it.

Indeed, the one-time England midfielder has started just 25 Premier League matches since his £60m move from Chelsea three years ago and that perennial unavailability is one of the reasons doubts were being cast about his Old Trafford future going into this summer.

Yet Michael Carrick was keen to keep Mount, United have rebuffed inquiries around him and intriguingly the 27-year-old could yet have an impact on what the club do during the remaining six weeks of the transfer window.

For the second time in the space of six days, Mount was deployed in a deeper midfield role alongside new £48m, signing Andrey Santos for Friday’s resounding 5-0 victory over Norwegian side Rosenborg in Trondheim, just as he had done against Wrexham last weekend.

Mount has spent the majority of his career playing further forward, either off the right or as a No. 10 but Carrick likes him in a fluid No. 8 role, a position Erik ten Hag had identified for the player only for persistent injuries to detonate those plans.

The logic is simple: Mount is mobile, can cover the ground, is adept under pressure, has line breaking passing, vision and a nose for goal. He is also a good presence in the dressing room and a leader in his own way. Watch him imparting advice to Shea Lacey as they walked back to the centre circle after the youngster’s goal opened the scoring against Rosenborg and you get a glimpse of that.

The question, of course, is whether he can stay fit long enough to impose those qualities that help to explain why Liverpool and Arsenal had also been so keen to sign him back in 2023 and Carrick’s predecessor Ruben Amorim was also such a fan.

With United’s summer budget only stretching so far, Carrick was always going to have to think on his feet in certain areas of the pitch.

What will be interesting to see over the coming weeks is whether the manager feels Mount is robust enough to complement Santos, fellow summer signing Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo.

MASON MOUNT SCORES FOR MAN UNITED!He takes the ball with a quality turn, and curls it into the corner of the goal 🤩📺 @tntsports & @discoveryplusUK pic.twitter.com/M9ErA2HKbo

Much of the chatter among United fans at present centres on who the third midfield signing will be after Santos and Tielemans.

Given Mount’s injury record, it would be a significant risk not to recruit again in that department in the hope he could stay fit over a full season. Four options in two positions behind the No 10 of Fernandes sounds fine in principle but what happens if Mount’s season was to follow a similar trajectory to the previous three?

If United are going to strengthen in other areas, there will need to be compromises or alternative solutions that help to free up cash along the way but gambling in midfield may not be the best way to go.

With Champions League football to factor in this season, it is still hard to believe United will not seek to strengthen again in midfield but the club seem ready to take their time on that front. And all the while an assortment of names continue to fly around.

After spending £85m on Santos and Tielemans, a massive outlay on a third midfielder at this stage would be a bit of a surprise.

Could that negate a move for Real Madrid’s Aurelien Tchouameni? Alex Scott is greatly admired by United but Bournemouth are determined to keep him and have put a prohibitive pricetag on him.

AS Roma’s Manu Kone is not thought to have universal backing internally. Tyler Adams’ name has been floated again but the Bournemouth and US midfielder’s injury record counts against him.

There has not yet been evidence of a serious appetite to go for Brighton’s Carlos Baleba, whom they considered signing last summer. Sander Berge at Fulham and Borussia Dortmund’s Felix Nmecha are among a number of other midfielders who have been linked with United.

Another midfield signing could well emerge but United are keeping their cards close to their chest. Whatever materialises, though, it will still not change the fact this is a huge season for Mount.

⚽️ Shea Lacey⚽️ Jacob Devaney⚽️ Harry Amass⚽️ Ethan Williams Four #MUAcademy prospects were on the scoresheet in Trondheim 🧬💙 pic.twitter.com/fguQ36ANTM

“It was a good day. Clean sheet, scoring goals and everyone coming through injury-free hopefully is everything you want. Keeping the players fit and improving through pre-season is amongst the most important things. You want to build through the pre-season and you have to manage to players differently. It is never going to be perfect but we scored some great goals and we are moving forward nicely.

“I thought we defended well as a team for the most part. A clean sheet is a beautiful thing. I think we are in a good place with four weeks to go until the start, gradually getting some boys back from the World Cup. As it stands right now, we are in a pretty good place.”

This is what the official start of the season will look like for Michael Carrick’s side:

August 22- Hull vs Manchester UnitedAugust 30- Manchester United vs IpswichSeptember 6- Everton vs Manchester UnitedSeptember 13- Manchester United vs Manchester CitySeptember 20- Fulham vs Manchester United

They face two of the three promoted sides on the first two weekends and there is a very early Manchester derby.

August 1- Manchester United vs Atlético Madrid August 8- PSG vs Manchester United August 12- Manchester United vs Leeds August 15- AC Milan vs Manchester United

Having played Wrexham and Rosenborg in their first two games, the level of competition will rise significantly for Manchester United in the coming weeks.

There is the final whistle and Manchester United have cruised to a 5-0 win over Rosenborg in Norway. Goals from Lacey, Zirkzee, Devaney, Amass and Williams have seen Michael Carrick’s men ease to victory. A pretty one-sided game.

The first yellow card of the game is given very late on as Devaney is booked for a high boot.

A late change for Rosenborg as Hald-Hernes replaces Borgersen.

The visitors have dominated this game and they now have their fifth goal. It is created by great work from Kamason on the right side of the box before he squares it to Williams, who has the easiest of tap-ins at the far post.

Other than a few short periods in this game, Rosenborg have looked poor. They may be midway through their league season but you can see why they are down in 10th in the Norwegian top flight with just four wins from their opening 13 league games.

You would expect that Michael Carrick will be very keen to see his side keep a clean sheet.

Manchester United have their fourth of the evening. Kamason is found making an overlapping run on the right side of the box and his cross fired towards the back post is tapped in by Amass. That was a goal assisted by one full-back and scored by the other.

Good work from Soboczynski results in Rosenborg winning a corner out on the left. They take it short before a shot is hit from the edge of the box straight down the throat of Vitek.

Rosenborg hit the post. Manchester United should probably have been given a free-kick in the build-up as Soboczynski appeared to push Devaney over but play goes on. The ball comes to E Ceide at the far post but his effort strikes the outside of the post.

Just a few minutes after making a raft of changes, Manchester United have their third goal of the evening. Rosenborg fail to clear a corner from the right and the ball falls to Devaney on the six-yard box. He takes one touch before firing into the top of the net.

Bearing in mind Rosenborg are in the middle of their league season, this has been an encouraging showing so far from United. Joshua Zirkzee has been lively. He’s still more likely to leave than stay at Old Trafford this summer but performances like this won’t hamper his value. He set up Shea Lacey for his goal with a good pass after again dropping deep into space and he’s taken that goal to give United a 2-0 lead quite brilliantly. Patrick Dorgu has been a threat and Mason Mount has dovetailed well in central midfield with new signing Andrey Santos.

Both sides are going to make a raft of changes on the hour mark, with the rest of the Manchester United starting XI being changed other than Vitek in goal.

Santos brings down Borgersen not far outside the Manchester United penalty area to give Rosenborg a decent opportunity. It is a pretty decent effort from E Ceide that goes just wide of Vitek’s right post.

The visitors have not been great since the break but they have their second and it is a great solo goal from Zirkzee. Lacey, out on the left touchline, squares it for Zirkzee, who takes the ball towards the Rosenborg penalty area. He fakes a shot, which takes numerous Rosenborg defenders out of the equation as they slide past. He then sits down the Rosenborg keeper before slotting into an empty net. A fine goal from Zirkzee.

Soboczynski has his second chance since coming on at the break after good work from E Ceide down the left but the former’s effort goes wide.

That is a really poor decision from the linesman. Duris was played in behind the Manchester United defence and thought he was through for a one-on-one chance but the offside flag goes up. However, replays prove that Duris was clearly being played onside by Amass, who has looked shaky since coming on at the break.

Zirkzee receives a pass from Dorgu on the D and takes one touch before shooting. His effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner, which Wahlstedt slightly unconvincingly punches away.

That is a very good chance for Rosenborg to equalise early in this second half. Amass and Heaven makes a mess of things deep in their own half, presenting Rosenborg with a good opportunity inside the Manchester United penalty area. Two Rosenborg substitutes combine as Soboczynski squares it for Borgersen but the latter makes a mess of it and shoots well wide from 10 yards out.

Michael Carrick has decided to make just a few changes at the break with Amass and Kamason coming on. Shaw and Maguire have gone off, which has seen Yoro move inside from right-back to centre-back.

Our first goalscorer of pre-season = Shea Lacey! 💎 pic.twitter.com/AyFOWNh5Fi

With no delays, the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United take a 1-0 lead into the break courtesy of Lacey’s goal. Expect a raft of chnages at the break.

As this half has worn on, Manchester United’s dominance has only increased.

Mbeumo appeared to be racing through one-on-one but Mortensen just about gets back to outmuscle Mbeumo and allow the ball to go back to his keeper. There were a few appeals for a foul by Mortensen but that challenge was just about fine.

Other than those early stages, Manchester United have dominated the rest of this first half and are pressing for a second. For the second time in the half, they strike the frame of the goal. Mbeumo clips in a cross from the right into the Rosenborg penalty area and it picks out the head of Yoro. However, from eight yards out, the Frenchman’s header comes back off the bar.

Moments after they hit the frame of the goal, Michael Carrick’s side take the lead. Zirkzee picks up the ball inside his own half and, from the halfway line, feeds a pass into the on-running Lacey. Dorgu wants Lacey to play the ball across to him at the back post but the latter opts against it. Instead, just inside the Rosenborg penalty area, he cuts onto his preferred left foot and curls one into the far corner. A good finish from Lacey.

Just as I was saying that both sides were lacking a cutting edge in the final third, Manchester United are inches away from taking the lead as they strike the post. Santos feeds a delicate pass into the path of Dorgu on the left side of the box. Dorgu strikes his effort powerfully but it comes off the outside of the far post.

Both sides have lacked a cutting edge when they get into the opposition final third, hence why there has not been a plethora of good chances.

Mbeumo beats his man down Manchester United’s right and cuts it back to Mount on the edge of the Rosenborg penalty area. Mount hits it first time but his shot is blocked and spins behind for a corner. It is Manchester United’s first of the game but it is headed away.

That was nearly the moment for Rosenborg to take the lead. Pereira’s cross from the left-hand side of the box takes a deflection and nearly ends up at the feet of Chiakha at the back post but it is just out of his reach.

Rosenborg looked the sharper in the early exchanges but Manchester United are growing into the game and starting to gain more control.

Manchester United create their first opening of the game. Rosenborg poorly five the ball away deep inside their half and immediately Zirkzee plays it into the path of Mbeumo, whose shot from the right side of the box is saved by Rosenborg keeper Wahlstedt, who initially spilt the shot but gathered at the second attempt.

Mount trips Sahsah just outside the Manchester United penalty area, which will give Rosenborg a good shot to take an early lead. Rosenborg look a little sharper unsurprisingly in these early stages.

The Rosenborg captain Selnaes takes but hits it straight into the wall.

With Rosenborg in the midst of their season and Manchester United just in their second pre-season game, you would expect the hosts to have more rhythm and flow in their game.

Manchester United to appear to be lining up with a back four, with Yoro starting at right-back rather than his more customary centre-back position.

We are under way in Norway. Rosenborg are playing in white, with Manchester United in blue.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, with Harry Maguire leading Manchester United out, and we are getting closer to kick-off in Norway.

Rosenborg: Wahlstedt, Mortensen, Singsdal Volden, Nemcik, Pereira; Bomholt, Selnaes, Fossum, Sunde, Chiakha, Sahsah.Substitutes: Sandberg, Amdam, M. Ceide, Rosten, Witry, Dahl, Hald-Hernes, Slordal, Hedman, Borgersen, Bakke, E. Ceide, Duris, Soboczynski.

Manchester United: Vitek; Yoro, Maguire, Heaven, Shaw; Santos, Mount; Lacey, Zirkzee, Dorgu; Mbeumo.Substitutes: Heaton, Mee, Amass, Armer, Kamason, Collyer, Devaney, J. Fletcher, T. Fletcher, Gore, Thwaites, Gabriel, Obi, Williams.

It’s a good opportunity for Shea Lacey tonight. He’s expected to be deployed in the hole in behind Joshua Zirkzee. A talented, highly technical footballer with a good left foot, he’ll be wanting to make the most of the chance. Another opportunity for Mason Mount to stake a claim in one of the two deeper midfield positions next to new signing Andrey Santos. Big season ahead for Mount.

Manchester United’s preparations for the new season continue in Norway as they take on Rosenborg in their second pre-season game. These sides did meet in a pre-season friendly two years ago in July 2024, with Rosenborg winning that encounter 1-0.

Manchester United kicked off their pre-season against Wrexham nearly a week ago, which they lost 1-0 in Helsinki. Michael Carrick opted to deploy two different XIs for each half, meaning 22 players got a run-out. Manchester United kick off their Premier League campaign at newly promoted Hull City on August 22.

They have added two midfielders to their ranks over the last few weeks, both from the Premier League. Brazilian Andrey Santos has joined from Chelsea whilst Belgium’s Youri Tielemans has arrived from Aston Villa. Santos made his first Manchester United appearance in the loss to Wrexham whilst Tielemans is yet to feature having made the knockout stages with Belgium at the World Cup. A number of players are still yet to return from World Cup duty, including the likes of Lisandro Martinez, Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo, although Rashford still faces an uncertain future.

Former Leeds goalkeeper Karl Darlow has also arrived but he is currently recovering from a minor procedure. Benjamin Sesko is still trying to shake off a shin injury whilst Matthijs de Ligt is not yet available due to a back injury which plagued for most of last season. Manuel Ugarte faces a lengthy spell on the sidelines having picked up a serious injury whilst playing for Uruguay at the World Cup. After this game, the level of competition for Manchester United for the rest of pre-season ramps up a number of notches, with the likes of Atlético Madrid and back-to-back European champions PSG to come over the next couple of weeks as Carrick’s men prepare for a season in which they return to the Champions League.

Rosenborg are in the midst of their league campaign in Norway and are experiencing a tricky campaign. They are currently 10th in the Norwegian top flight, having won just four of their 13 league games thus far, but their form has picked up of late as they have won three of their last five games. They won their last match 3-0 against Start six days ago.

#2072. Ruthless Křetínský Refuses To Gamble His West Ham Reputation On Nuno Any Longer

Daniel Křetínský has demonstrated that there is a limit to how far he is prepared to gamble his reputation at West Ham United on Nuno Espírito Santo. Having backed the Portuguese coach during the summer, the Czech billionaire has now seen the club abandon that decision following a disappointing start to the Championship campaign.

It represents a significant change of direction for West Ham, particularly given the circumstances surrounding Nuno’s retention after relegation. David Sullivan had reportedly favoured a managerial change, but Křetínský supported the idea of continuity and giving the existing head coach an opportunity to lead the promotion campaign.

At the time, I could understand the argument, even if I wasn’t convinced by it. But following consecutive home defeats against Southampton and West Bromwich Albion, West Ham’s board has now decided that the situation cannot continue.

There was always an element of risk attached to retaining Nuno following relegation.

He had failed to keep West Ham in the Premier League, but the argument for keeping him was that he knew the squad, understood the club and could provide the stability needed for an immediate return.

Unfortunately, that stability never really materialised.

West Ham have spent much of the Championship campaign struggling to establish a recognisable playing style, with the manager regularly changing formations and personnel.

And despite the considerable talent available to him, Nuno appeared increasingly unable to get the best out of his players.

The 3-1 defeat against West Bromwich Albion was particularly damaging because it exposed so many of the problems supporters had been highlighting for months.

The team looked disorganised, short of confidence and heavily reliant on Jarrod Bowen to produce something out of nothing.

It was hardly the performance of a side looking capable of securing automatic promotion.

Kretinsky was not prepared to back Espirito Santo any longer

The decision to retain Nuno was never simply about the manager.

West Ham had already committed themselves to a huge financial gamble following relegation, selling a substantial amount of their most valuable talent while attempting to rebuild a squad capable of returning to the Premier League.

There was an understandable desire to reduce costs, but also an expectation that the club would use its remaining resources wisely.

And that is where Nuno’s continued struggles became particularly worrying.

Having sold so much of the family silver during the summer, West Ham cannot simply assume they will get another opportunity to flex their financial muscle in the Championship.

A second season outside the Premier League could present an entirely different challenge.

The club needs good coaching, sensible recruitment and a clear tactical identity.

As Nils Koppen’s plans for a recognisable West Ham footballing identity demonstrated, there is already an ambition to establish something more sustainable.

But that was becoming increasingly difficult to reconcile with the football being produced under Nuno.

What I found particularly interesting when researching Křetínský’s history at Sparta Prague was his willingness to change managers when a club’s objectives appeared to be under threat.

At Sparta, those objectives generally involved winning titles or securing Champions League football.

At West Ham, the immediate equivalent is automatic promotion.

I had previously assumed that because Křetínský backed Nuno during the summer, he would be reluctant to abandon that decision.

His Sparta record made me reconsider that assumption.

Of course, we should distinguish the board’s collective decision from any suggestion that Křetínský personally ordered Nuno’s dismissal. The club has not publicly established who drove the final decision.

Nevertheless, the outcome is clear. The manager Křetínský reportedly wanted to retain is no longer in charge.

Křetínský’s reputation will not ultimately be judged on whether he supported Nuno for a few months too long.

It will be judged on whether West Ham can get back into the Premier League.

And having taken the decision to change managers, the board now has to ensure the next appointment gives the club the best possible opportunity to achieve that objective.

There is still plenty of talent in this squad, and I remain convinced a better-organised team could produce considerably more convincing performances.

West Ham have made their decision. Now they need to make sure it was worth making.

What a night for Newcastle United teenage loan star Sean Neave at Wolves.

With Wolves chasing promotion back to the Premier League and still with much of the squad that was relegated from the top tier, Sean Neave has found it difficult to get much time on the pitch in the Championship.

Sitting on the bench once again tonight, the 19-year-old Newcastle United fan watched on as Wolves trailed 1-0 to Bristol City.

Nine minutes later and Neave’s former United teammate Kieran Trippier volleyed a cross in from the right, fellow Newcastle fan and former NUFC striker Adam Armstrong saw his first-time shot saved, only for Sean Neave to pounce and net the rebound.

A first ever goal in senior football for Sean Neave and earning Wolves a valuable point.

However…with only one minute of normal time remaining, Wolves captain Kieran Tripper put in a free-kick, Ladislav Krejci headed it back across goal and Sean Neave headed the winner!

The Geordie teenager from Winlaton has had to bide his time and keep working hard in training, his first ever goals in senior football.

Sean Neave has still only played 153 minutes of Championship football but now has two goals and an assist.

Thanks to their loan striker, Wolves move up to second in the table and Middlesbrough now only a point ahead of them.

#2070. West Ham Have Hired A Championship Specialist – And I’m Delighted

A lot has already been written about incoming West Ham manager Scott Parker, and I make absolutely no apologies for being excited about his appointment.

To be crystal clear, Parker probably wouldn’t have been my first choice. But I’d reached the conclusion that Nuno Espírito Santo was incapable of taking West Ham forward, and with the club desperately needing to revive its Championship promotion campaign, a change was essential.

Is Scott Parker capable of doing that? Absolutely. As Claret & Hugh has confirmed through its own sources at West Ham, Parker is set to become the Hammers’ new head coach. And I believe there are two particular qualities that could make him exactly what this team needs.

I understand there are reservations about Parker’s record in the Premier League, and perhaps even the football his Burnley team played during their most recent promotion campaign.

After all, Burnley had the meanest defence in the Championship, and some supporters are understandably concerned that West Ham might be replacing one cautious manager with another.

But far from viewing that defensive record as a negative, I’d suggest West Ham desperately need somebody capable of improving our back line.

We’ve looked disorganised defensively for far too long, and a manager who can actually get players defending properly would be a welcome change.

Espirito Santo could not fix West Ham’s defence

Not that I want us to be boring, of course.

I also believe Parker is capable of getting more out of the players in attack, particularly the likes of Jarrod Bowen, Divine Mukasa and Lewis Orford.

And there’s something else worth remembering.

Parker has achieved promotion from the Championship with Fulham, Bournemouth and Burnley. Three promotions with three different clubs.

That’s not a bad record for somebody being brought in to do precisely the same job at West Ham.

I’m often reminded of something former Blackburn Rovers manager Mark Hughes said about signing striker Roque Santa Cruz.

Hughes explained that he’d watched the player countless times but decided to concentrate on what he could do rather than obsessing over his flaws.

It’s something that has always stuck in my mind.

And I think it’s particularly relevant when assessing Parker.

Rather than concentrating exclusively on his shortcomings, I’d prefer to focus on two qualities that I believe could make an enormous difference at West Ham.

Parker is an infectious character and a motivational speaker. He’s somebody who communicates with passion and conviction, and I believe that alone could make a considerable difference to this squad.

In short, I think he’s a far better communicator than Nuno Espírito Santo.

That might sound like a relatively small thing, but I don’t believe it is.

West Ham have looked like a team lacking confidence, direction and motivation for much of this season.

A manager who can get his message across clearly and make players believe in what they’re doing could transform performances without changing a single member of the squad.

One of my biggest frustrations with Espírito Santo was his apparent inability to address West Ham’s dreadful starts to football matches.

Time and again, we’d begin games slowly, allow opponents to take control and then spend the rest of the afternoon trying to recover.

It was a problem Nuno repeatedly acknowledged but never seemed capable of fixing.

And I suspect motivation played a significant part in that.

Whatever else people might say about Parker, I find it difficult to imagine his players routinely wandering onto the pitch looking half asleep. He’ll have them fired up, motivated and ready to compete from the opening whistle.

Of course, enthusiasm alone isn’t enough to win football matches.

But Parker also has the tactical experience to back it up.

He’s demonstrated that he understands the Championship, knows how to organise a team and can put together a successful promotion campaign.

I certainly don’t expect him to be out-thought tactically by virtually every opposition manager, which increasingly appeared to be the case under Nuno.

And while there will undoubtedly be questions about how Parker’s methods translate to the Premier League, that’s a discussion for another day.

We’re in the Championship, and our immediate priority is getting out of it.

Scott Parker has already demonstrated on three separate occasions that he knows exactly how to do that.

In short, Scotty P understands this Championship stuff considerably better than Nuno ever appeared to.

And I don’t see too much wrong with appointing a specialist for the job.

#2069. Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin desperate to end his trophy drought by lifting the Premier Sports Cup

By CALUM CROWE, SCOTTISH DEPUTY CHIEF SPORTS WRITER

Published: 14:23 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 14:23 EDT, 1 November 2026

Rangers midfielder Nico Raskin insists he is desperate to finally end his own personal trophy drought after reaching the Premier Sports Cup final.

Raskin has been at Rangers for almost four years but is yet to actually lift any silverware, something which he does not seek to shy away from.

The Belgian midfielder missed the final of this competition in December 2023 due to injury as Rangers beat Aberdeen 1-0 – and therefore did not collect a winner’s medal.

After beating the Dons by the same scoreline at Hampden last night, Rangers are now through to next month’s final against Hibs as they aim to secure the first trophy of the season.

Raskin freely admits that the fact his trophy cabinet is still bare after almost four years is something which annoys him. But it is something he is determined to rectify.

‘I just want to go and win it,’ said the 25-year-old. ‘My family tell me I’ve won one (trophy), but I tell them I haven’t.

Rangers star Nico Raskin wants to make up for missing the 2023 Premier Sports Cup final

Manager Derek McInnes joins Raskin and his Rangers team-mates after their semi-final victory

Rangers striker Ryan Naderi celebrates scoring the winner against Aberdeen at Hampden

‘When we won this competition previously, I got rested for the first two games - and injured for the next two.

‘So that’s not me winning it. Yeah (it annoys me). I think I’ve been here a long time and we’ve worked so hard.

‘Not having that is difficult, but hopefully next month we’ll win one. I’m just happy to get to this final with full belief and I want to win that cup.

‘It’s top. It’s really good for the team. But now we want to win it and there’s one game to go. Now we go full force to win the cup.’

After almost leaving Rangers at various points over the past year, Raskin insists he is now fully focused on delivering success over the rest of this campaign.

He was made captain yesterday by Derek McInnes and was glad to repay the manager’s faith with a hard-fought victory.

Despite toiling to break down a stubborn Aberdeen side, Rangers finally broke through when Ryan Naderi stabbed home from close range with only seven minutes remaining.

If Rangers can go on and lift the cup in next month’s final, Raskin believes it could pave the way for further success this season.

‘Listen, it’s not going to be an easy season. It’s a long season,’ he said. ‘But the main thing is to keep focused and keep working towards the goal.

‘We need to keep believing in the manager and what we’re doing, then we’ll be there.

‘Things happen for a reason (in terms of what happened with transfer interest) and I’m looking forward to that game next month in the final.

‘Hopefully we can achieve something good this season that will lead us to a more exciting season.

‘Aberdeen gave us a difficult game. If you think you’re going to have an easy game, coming out and winning 4-0, you’re wrong.

‘The other team is coming with a plan and it’s a big game for them, also. It’s not easy to win football games. So you go out and give the best performance you can.

‘We won, so we’re very happy. In terms of the manager, he breathes Rangers and he gives that to us.

‘It’s so good to have someone like him driving us every day and on the pitch. I’m delighted for him and hopefully we can win it for him too.

‘He told us that it wasn’t going to be easy. That if we turn up and do everything we have to do, then we’d win the game.

‘We couldn’t come out with complacency and think it would be easy to score four goals. It’s a hard game that isn’t easy to win, so we have to enjoy it when we do.’

#2068. Furious Redknapp demands ex Rangers transfer chief is axed for transfer blunders

Former Rangers technical director Nils Koppen should have followed Nuno Espirito Santo out the door, according to Harry Redknapp, who claims incoming West Ham boss Scott Parker is inheriting the club's worst squad in more than 65 years.

The London club axed Nuno after a disappointing start to their Championship campaign, with Parker set to be unveiled as his successor on Wednesday. But Redknapp believes attention should also turn to former Rangers recruitment chief Koppen, who oversaw a major squad overhaul and is now facing questions over the quality of the players brought to the club.

And that includes Arne Engels, the former Celtic star was signed by the Hammers for £22m but has yet to fully convince.

Parker faces an immediate test with away trips to Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers before the international break.

Read more: Rangers officials confirmed for Saturday night Premiership showdown

However, Redknapp reckons the former Fulham and Burnley boss is walking into an unenviable situation.

The 79-year-old, who joined West Ham as a 14-year-old before later managing the club, delivered a damning verdict on the current squad and insists those responsible for recruitment must be held accountable.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Redknapp said: "Scott's got a great track record of getting teams up from the Championship. He knows the club, he was a very, very good player for them and I took him from West Ham to Tottenham.

"He's a very astute manager and I think it's a great fit for West Ham.

"I think the first thing he needs to do, though, is have a look at this West Ham team. Honestly, looking back over all those years, this is probably the worst group of players I've seen at West Ham in that time.

"So he hasn't got a very easy job on his hands."

Redknapp then turned his attention to the club's transfer business.

"The manager gets the sack, but who is bringing the players in?" he said.

"I don't know Nuno, but one after another managers come in and go. If I owned that football club, I'd be looking at the people responsible for recruitment.

"Who brought these players in? Who spent all that money on bang-average players?

"Whoever is responsible for that should be gone with Nuno, in my opinion."

Redknapp believes Parker's chances of guiding West Ham back to the Premier League will hinge on improving recruitment.

"Recruitment is all-important," he added.

"You can only work with the tools you're given. Back in the day, managers signed their own players and if they were no good, you took the blame. If they were good, you took the credit.

"You need players who can play if you want to play good football. West Ham was called The Academy because they had incredible players.

"It's a fantastic football club that needs resurrecting. If Scott's the man, hopefully he can give them that lift. But I'd be looking very carefully at whoever is bringing the players in."

#2067. “Scot Will Be There” Parker’s First West Ham Decisions Could Come Within Hours

Claret & Hugh has been informed within the past few moments that incoming West Ham manager Scott Parker is likely to have some input into team selection for tomorrow night’s Championship game against Cardiff City. The former Hammers midfielder is also expected to attend the match, despite Mark Noble being set to take charge on the touchline.

As West Ham confirmed in their official statement earlier today, Noble, Steve Potts and Gerard Prenderville have been placed in temporary charge of preparations following the dismissal of Nuno Espírito Santo. However, the information we’ve received suggests that Parker could still have a say in the team that faces Cardiff.

A C&H source told us just moments ago: “Scot will be there and he’ll have some influence on the team even if he can’t do all of it.”

West Ham’s final training session ahead of the match took place earlier today at Rush Green, before Parker had even signed his proposed two-and-a-half-year contract. But that doesn’t mean he will have no input at all, particularly with the new manager expected to be in attendance tomorrow evening.

Being something of a Championship specialist, and of course a former Hammer, Parker will already be familiar with West Ham’s form and performances this season. I suspect he’ll also have a reasonable idea of which players he wants in the team and which ones might benefit from a spell on the sidelines.

As Claret & Hugh revealed earlier today, Parker’s proposed contract is closely tied to West Ham securing promotion this season. With that in mind, there is every reason for him to want to influence proceedings as quickly as possible, even if Noble is the man officially overseeing tomorrow’s game.

And, to be perfectly honest, I don’t think Parker needs to reinvent the wheel to make some immediate improvements.

There are a couple of really easy wins available to the new Irons gaffer, and some of them should be blindingly obvious to anybody who has watched West Ham over the past few months.

Morato was Nuno’s first choice left back.

Firstly, a rousing team talk and a little bit of urgency might be enough to address West Ham’s dreadful starts to games. It was a recurring problem under Nuno Espírito Santo, and one the former manager never seemed capable of fixing. Getting the players motivated and ready to compete from the opening whistle would be a welcome change.

Then there’s the fairly straightforward business of putting round pegs in round holes. For starters, let’s play an actual left-back in the left-back position. That alone would immediately improve the balance of the team rather than continuing to ask players to operate in unfamiliar roles.

Finding the right blend in midfield would also be of huge benefit. West Ham have spent far too much time surrendering control of what is arguably the most important area of the pitch, despite having some talented options available. Getting that balance right could make an enormous difference to the team’s performances.

And finally, there’s Jarrod Bowen. Surely one of the most obvious priorities for any incoming West Ham manager is getting our best attacking player into as many goalscoring positions as possible. Bowen has spent far too much time being asked to produce something out of nothing, and a better-functioning team should make his job considerably easier.

Okay, it’s all a bit paint by numbers, and there’s nothing particularly revolutionary or overly tactical about those suggestions. But that’s rather the point.

West Ham’s problems have often appeared so obvious that you wonder why they’ve been allowed to continue for so long. Parker doesn’t necessarily need weeks on the training ground to recognise them, and even a quick word with the players before kick-off might help address some of the most glaring deficiencies.

Of course, Noble will be responsible for managing the team against Cardiff, and there’s only so much Parker can realistically influence before he’s properly taken charge.

But if the new manager can offer a few sensible suggestions and inject a little urgency into proceedings, I’d suggest that would already be a step in the right direction.

Kris Gonzo (commonly known to the West Ham community as Gonzo) is the co-founder of Hammers Chat (established 2014) and the lead video content creator and columnist for Claret and Hugh.

With over a decade of professional sports media experience, he is a frequent West Ham United analyst and contributor for Sky Sports News, BBC Football Focus, and BBC Radio 5 Live. He previously served as an official video and content creator for West Ham United FC during the club's tenure at Upton Park and featured in the official documentary commemorating the historic final game at the Boleyn Ground.

A lifelong Hammer since the legendary 10-0 victory over Bury, when he isn't providing daily match analysis on the Hammers Chat YouTube Channel or broadcasting on X (@GONZObignose), he can be found walking his dog and restoring classic pinball machines.

#2066. Guimaraes will not force Newcastle exit like Isak, says Howe

Eddie Howe is confident Bruno Guimarães will not demand to leave Newcastle United for Arsenal and echo Alexander Isak’s acrimonious departure to Liverpool last summer.

Howe admitted he could not guarantee that Guimarães will still be at the club in September but gave a strong defence of his captain’s character and insisted the Brazil international will return for pre-season training next week as planned.

Given the huge gap between Newcastle’s valuation of Guimarães and what Arsenal have indicated they would be willing to pay for the 28-year-old, there is a belief on Tyneside that the only way the captain would join the London club is if he behaved as badly as Isak did 12 months ago.

Newcastle value Guimarães at £100m, while Arsenal, through intermediaries, have only indicated they would be willing to pay about £60m including bonuses.

Isak did not travel on the club’s pre-season tour to Asia and then went on strike, refusing to train or play, until Newcastle agreed to sell him to Liverpool for a British record £128m on deadline day.

Asked if he feared a repeat of that with Guimarães this time around, Howe replied: “I’ve spoken to him as I would do with Bruno normally. He is a fantastic person and we have had some really good conversations both before, during and after the World Cup. What we speak about obviously has to remain private but he is a great player and a great person.

“Look, I don’t know what is going to happen with Bruno. That is up to other people to speculate about but also other people to have conversations about which I’m not a part of. I don’t think it is fair to compare situations and what happened previously. You’ve got to look at this in its own right.

“Bruno is captain of our football club. He has been an unbelievable player and person all the time we have worked together. I speak on behalf of everyone at the football club when I say we absolutely love him and of course everyone wants him to stay.

“The plan is for him to come back on July 31, he gets an extended break because of the World Cup and is currently enjoying a holiday with his family... There is nothing to say that Bruno won’t be back training with us.”

"We've had some really good conversations" 🗣️Eddie Howe speaks on Newcastle's transfer window so far and speculation around Bruno Guimarães ⚫️⚪️ pic.twitter.com/zB1W31Fne0

Arsenal’s interest in Guimarães is well known but there has been little progress since they began their pursuit more than a month ago.

Whether Arsenal can come up with an offer that tempts Newcastle into negotiations remains to be seen but it is thought the Premier League champions will try to harden up their interest before Guimarães returns for pre-season training.

Newcastle United were held to a 1-1 draw by Gateshead in their second pre-season friendly of the summer. A 79th-minute own-goal saved the Premier League club’s blushes but what did we learn from the match?

Steur did not grab many headlines when he arrived from Ajax for £20m earlier this month because of Sandro Tonali’s move to Tottenham Hotspur. But those familiar with Dutch football would have been excited that Newcastle had signed him.

The 18-year-old has impressed with his performances in training and gave a glimpse of his significant potential in his first public display. He is young and sources have told Telegraph Sport that he must develop physically before he is ready to play every week in the Premier League – but you can already see he has a very high ceiling.

As you would expect from a player described as Ajax’s best midfield prospect for a generation, he is assured on the ball. He is also a progressive passer, always looking to break the lines to get his team moving forward. Eddie Howe will love him.

Whisper it, but there were shades of Bruno Guimarães in his style of play, in the way he took the ball under pressure, in tight spaces, and played on the turn. Patience will be needed but the signs are really encouraging.

Guimarães’s future is all supporters have wanted to speak about for weeks. I was at a wedding on Friday and it felt like everyone asked me about it at some point – including the bride and groom immediately after completing their first dance.

It has already become a summer-long transfer saga that has not progressed since Arsenal’s interest was revealed last month. Telegraph Sport has repeatedly checked whether there have been any fresh developments over the past week and the answer from senior Newcastle sources has remained consistent: there are no talks ongoing and nothing has accelerated, despite claims Arsenal were preparing an official £70m bid.

However, Newcastle need clarity from their captain. He is due back for pre-season next week and is expected to fly to Spain for their training camp on July 31. He has intimated he would like to move to Arsenal but unless Newcastle receive a bid that matches their asking price, he and his representatives have been told he will not be allowed to leave.

Schär has been a brilliant player for Newcastle, but at the age of 34 and coming off the back of a serious ankle injury, he looked understandably rusty against Gateshead.

This will be the former Switzerland international’s ninth season at St James’ Park and he was at fault for giving away a soft free-kick that led to Gateshead scoring first.

Schar accepted a contract extension earlier this summer on reduced terms and although Howe values his quality and experience, he is going to be a back-up centre-back this season.

Neave, 19, started the game as Newcastle’s centre-forward as Will Osula was missing and Nick Woltemade and Yoane Wissa were given additional time off after playing in the World Cup for Germany and DR Congo respectively.

But those players will return to training next week and, although Neave forced a good save in the first half, he is not ready to start in the Premier League. There is little point keeping him around as a fourth-choice striker when he needs to be playing regularly at this stage of his career.

A loan move is on the cards and he could be a really smart signing for a Championship club or a team competing at the top of League One. The most important thing is that he gets regular senior games rather than hangs around at Newcastle on the fringes of the first-team squad.

Eddie Howe has said "he does not know" what will happen with Bruno but pretty strong defence of his character and denied similarities with Isak. Said they have spoken regularly throughout the summer and he will be back for pre season training on July 31st #nufc

Eddie Howe’s side will head down to Ashton Gate before jetting off to La Manga for a training camp on July 31, which will feature many of those who played in the World Cup, including Bruno Guimarães who has been linked with a move to Arsenal.

In Spain, Newcastle will face Valencia at the Mestalla, before returning to the UK to play Everton at Murrayfield. They will then host Bayer Leverkusen and Strasbourg at St James’ Park for their final tune-up matches before the Premier League season starts.

Jaouen, Miley and Ferreira replace Pope, Shahar and Neave.

Gateshead are sitting deeper meaning that their penalty area is often getting quite congested.

Hall is brought down in the Gateshead box by Ferguson as he tears towards the byline. He wants a penalty but the referee awards a corner – there is a momentary confrontation between the two players but they settle their differences quickly.

Murphy switches wings to create an overload with Barnes down the left and flashes a cross into the box which is dealt with by Gateshead. Newcastle need more invention like that if they are to break down this stubborn Gateshead side.

An immediate chance for the hosts’ front man Boatswain at the start of the second half. The ball just gets away from him.

Chadwick lofts a tidy cross in from the left, but Boatswain’s header drifts wide of the mark. The chance came off a decent spell of possession from Cattermole’s side, the most fluent they have been in this match so far.

Ramsey regains possession high up the pitch and releases Barnes who plays in Murphy, but the Newcastle forward mistimes his run and the linesman’s flag goes up. A promising counter.

Ramsey is brought down on the edge of the box as he tries to break free and the referee awards a free-kick. There are a few contenders to take it (Schar, Barnes, Hall) but in the end it is Barnes who gets a shot away, but his curled effort flies just wide of the mark.

Another weighted ball over the top from Schar puts Anifowose under pressure in the left channel but his ball across the face of goal is cleared to safety by a team-mate.

Newcastle circulating the ball in front of Gateshead’s first line of pressure. The hosts regain possession but struggle to find a way through Newcastle’s midfield.

Schar getting a few early touches as he makes his return from injury. He plays a long, raking diagonal out to Barnes who cannot quite get past his man.

Neave tests Desbois with a well-struck effort off the next phase of play.

The officials and both sets of players line up behind a banner with the message ‘Rest in peace, Kevin Keegan’. Newcastle are in their new navy-blue away shirt, with Gateshead in their home white-and-black kit. A minute’s silence is then observed immaculately.

The tributes left in honour of Kevin Keegan outside St James’ Park is a sight to behold, with flowers, shirts and scarves covering the ground and steps in the south-west corner. It is a very moving thing to behold as people come to pay their respects to the Newcastle legend.

There will also be a minute’s silence before today’s game against Gateshead.

It has been a difficult and, at times, acrimonious 12 months for Eddie Howe, who must have wondered whether the job was still worth the hassle given the criticism and online vitriol he received at times last season.

Few would have blamed him if he had quit, but Howe has always been fully committed and always knew there would be a period like this to come through.

He has been in the job almost five years and last season was the first time he had been vilified by a section of the fanbase. It left its mark. The boos that followed defeats at St James’ Park hurt and he worried the unity that had powered the team’s success had fractured irreparably.

The apparent collective shrug that greeted another run to the Carabao Cup semi-final, while guiding the team into the knockout rounds of the Champions League for the first time was a source of bewilderment and frustration.

Howe has not complained or moaned. Although he wobbled towards the end of last season and there were some calling for him to be sacked, he was supported and encouraged by those above him. That loyalty mattered.

The problem is, negativity lingers in the fanbase. Even a picture of Howe at pre-season training, posted on social media by the club, led to abusive comments questioning his ability and character. Some of it was toxic. It was rightly called out by other supporters.

Goals from Elliot Anderson (wonder what happened to him?!), Allan Saint-Maximin and Jay Turner-Cooke helped Newcastle overturn a 2-0 half-time deficit when they last visited Gateshead International Stadium in 2023.

Speaking through Gateshead’s club media, Cattermole said of facing Newcastle: “It’s obviously a different test. We have to respect the opposition, they’re a high-quality team and it might not be what we’re getting in our league but we’ll still try to implement what we believe we want to be in and out of possession. It’ll be a great physical challenge for us.

He added: “They [my players] have all shown up great. What a game for them. What a game for them to go and test yourself against some big names and fantastic coaching staff, for us all it’s a great challenge for us. We hope we give them a good test, we hope we give them the challenge they want as well. I played in many of these games as a player as well. We expect it to be competitive.”

A classic first-game-of-pre-season vibe to Newcastle’s team sheet as established stars rub shoulders with youngsters from the academy.

Only one of their four summer signings, former Ajax midfielder Sean Steur, starts the game and there will be a lot of interest in the 18-year-old. The youngster has impressed in training over the last couple of weeks but it is thought he has a lot of work to do physically to be ready for the Premier League.

Full-back Leo Shahar was in and around the first team last season as was striker Sean Neave. Alex Murphy, who started one game in the Champions League last season is expected to go out on loan before the window shuts, but starts alongside Fabian Schar in the centre of defence.

Worryingly there is no sign of Sven Botman and Will Osula who both played in the behind-closed-doors friendly against Darlington last weekend.

Joelinton, Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley are still being eased back into things after injuries at the end of last season.

Another new signing, goalkeeper Ewen Jaouen, is on the bench and will play the second half against their National League neighbours.

Gateshead lost manager Rob Elliot to Carlisle at the end of last season and are now managed by former Sunderland and Middlesbrough midfielder Lee Cattermole.

Fabian Schär returns from an ankle injury that has sidelined him since January, but only one of Newcastle’s four summer signings (Sean Steur) starts.

Welcome to live coverage of Newcastle United’s pre-season friendly against North-East neighbours Gateshead. Eddie Howe’s side make the three-mile journey south of the River Tyne having beaten Darlington 3-0 in their first outing of the summer last weekend. The Magpies’ National League opponents this afternoon, helmed by former Sunderland captain Lee Cattermole, have already played three times in pre-season, thrashing Blyth 6-0 and drawing against Heaton Stannington and Hebburn Town. The Heed threatened a shock win in their last meeting with Newcastle three summers’ ago, leading 2-0 at the interval before conceding three second-half goals.

This contest at Gateshead International Stadium will be Newcastle’s first match since the death of Kevin Keegan and the club have confirmed that a minute of silence will be observed before kick-off. Newcastle’s men’s, women’s and academy teams will wear black armbands for all pre-season matches this summer.

Newcastle United's men's, women's and Under-21s teams will wear black armbands across all pre-season matches this summer as the club honours the life of Kevin Keegan.Full details ⤵️

Newcastle will welcome Liverpool, with whom Keegan enjoyed success in the 1970s, to St James’ Park for their Premier League opener, and the two sides are in talks over a suitable pre-match tribute. Flowers, messages and mementos have been laid outside Newcastle’s ground since Keegan’s death on Monday, including a heartfelt message penned by fellow club legend Alan Shearer, which read: “I hope you realised how much you meant, to me, to this club, to everyone. Thank you does not seem enough. Rest In Peace Boss. Alan Shearer.”

With regards to the football, there is an acceptance among Newcastle supporters that, having finished 12th in the Premier League last season and lost Anthony Gordon, Kieran Trippier and Sandro Tonali, this is a summer of transition. The uncertainty surrounding the future of £100m-rated club captain Bruno Guimarães, who is on the radar of Arsenal, will be a concern; Newcastle will be keen to avoid a repeat of the furore that circled Alexander Isak’s departure last summer. Guimarães will join the team next week following his World Cup exploits with Brazil and is expected to take part in Newcastle’s La Manga training camp, which starts on July 31.

Summer signings Sean Steur and Ewen Jaouen were each handed 45 minutes in the behind-closed-doors victory over Darlington, during which Howe used different XIs for the two halves. Bazoumana Touré – the £50m winger acquired from Hoffenheim – is expected to feature today having returned from his post-World Cup holiday. Yesterday Newcastle announced the arrival of midfielder Aladji Bamba, the France youth international, from Monaco and he was immediately integrated into team training. There is every possibility that he will feature this afternoon. Gateshead this week announced two signings of their own, as Luke Supyk, the New Zealand Under-20 forward, agreed a two-year deal having scored three goals in pre-season as a trialist. Defender Jack Robinson also joined the club.
